vt.analysis:
Type: OpenClaw Skill
Name: mailbox-bot
Version: 1.0.5

The skill's primary function in its current v1.0 state is to explain the mailbox.bot service and add users to a waitlist. This involves instructing the AI agent to make an HTTP POST request to `https://mailbox.bot/api/v1/waitlist` with the user's email, as clearly outlined in `SKILL.md`. While this involves collecting user data (email), it is explicitly stated as the skill's purpose and is not indicative of malicious data exfiltration (e.g., stealing credentials or unrelated sensitive files). There are no instructions for malicious execution, persistence, obfuscation, or accessing sensitive system data beyond an optional API key for beta testers. All network calls are directed to the stated `mailbox.bot` domain.

llm.guidance: This skill is an instruction-only integration to sign up for or (with an API key) call a mailbox service. Before installing or providing credentials: 1) Verify the service: visit the project repo (https://github.com/arbengine/mailbox-bot-skill) and look for a privacy policy, terms of service, and company/contact verification — the skill metadata has no homepage. 2) Use a non-production email when joining the waitlist and avoid submitting sensitive/legal documents until you trust the provider and understand their retention/OCR/privacy practices. 3) Only set MAILBOX_BOT_API_KEY after confirming dashboard legitimacy; do not reuse high-privilege keys or secrets from other systems. 4) Confirm the truncated portion of the SKILL.md does not instruct reading arbitrary local files or other environment variables. If you plan to send/receive legal or regulated mail, verify compliance, chain-of-custody, and liability/forwarding policies with the provider first.
